label: Oppy’s natural causal reality…: Causal reality includes every causal relatum
term: Oppy’s natural causal reality, restricted worlds and primitive ontological necessities
definition: Causal reality includes every causal relatum; Oppy proposes that natural reality exhausts it. His possible worlds share actual laws and some initial history and diverge through objective chance. He leaves a unique natural initial cause versus infinite regress open. In the restricted general-causal comparison, he balances commitments against explanatory breadth/depth and treats ontological necessities as primitives.
note: Source-specific proposal, not a proved metaphysically exhaustive modal semantics. Necessary initial state, particular state or aspect are alternative formulations in §VI; no rigid individual identity is inferred from a shared description. Necessity is not defined as independence, full explanation, cognitive access or divine attributes. The causal-priority and no-cycle principles in §I and the controversial necessity-to-independence step in §VI are Oppy’s arguments, not imported axioms here. See docs/notes/ultimate-explanation-and-knowledge-737.md.
